title: The Rene kids' brass band repertoire and Rene's playing
summary: The Tulane played patriotic marches by hand; Rene's kids played juke music; Rene was a sweet cornet player but afraid to travel.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Did the Tulane play anything by hand at all?

Well they played a few numbers. Like, you know, like the band playing now. They played a few numbers by hand. But those days, they mostly, mostly played patriotic band. Six eights and all that. That's what the brass band played.
But what about the Rene brass band, the kids? Did they play patriotic numbers too? By hand? Well no. They couldn't play patriotic. They couldn't cut it, huh?

No, they couldn't cut no patriotic. Because none of them know about the rhythm. So what would they play? They'd play just juke music. Music and all different sounds. Just regular old tongue numbers and stuff like that.
Yeah, tongue numbers. Could Rene play very high then? High? When he was a kid?
Well, he could play a little bit high, but none might. But to go at it, to tell you about the facts. Rene was a better corner player than the assumption.
Well, he had a couple years on him and that was important in those days, huh? You mean later on too? Oh no. No, when they were coming. Yeah, when they were coming, huh? Yeah, when they were coming.

Yeah, Rene was weak on the cliff. My boy had that. But Rene was scared to travel. See, he didn't go nowhere down. His brother was playing drum behind him. He left with his breath. And they stuck together. Yeah, I tell you. He drank his stuff. I think I drank a drink. Wow.
Wow. Wow. Wow. Wow. Wow. Wow. Wow. that night. He didn't, you know, he didn't try too hard most of the time but he really came out with some good stuff when he wanted to.
No, no, but if he was a sweet corner, his dad was a sweet man. He played song. Song and sweet.
